claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**To begin, could you tell me:**

1. **How many children** are you asking about for Child Benefit?
2. **What are their ages** or dates of birth?

This will help me understand which eligibility rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit rules differ depending on whether children are under 16, between 16-19, or 20 and over.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about one child - my son Alex. He's 19 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 19 years old.

Since Alex is between 16-19, I need to check some additional criteria. At this age, he needs to meet specific education or training requirements to qualify.

**Let me navigate to the next check:**

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In education or training** (such as school, college, university, or approved training scheme)?
2. **Recently left education** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Please let me know which applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So Alex is currently in education at sixth form college studying for A-levels.

Let me check the next requirement for his age and education status:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to verify a few details about Alex's education to ensure it meets the Child Benefit requirements:

**About Alex's A-level studies, please confirm:**

1. **Is this full-time education** with at least 12 hours per week of supervised study? (A-levels at sixth form college are typically full-time, but I need to confirm)

2. **Is the funding employer-funded** or is it standard education through the college? (This matters for eligibility)

3. **Is Alex married?** (This is relevant for the 16-19 age group)

Once I confirm these details, I can move forward with the assessment!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, it's full-time education - he's there during the week like a normal college schedule with proper supervised classes and coursework.

No, it's not employer-funded - it's just standard sixth form college education.

And no, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for confirming those details. Alex's situation is clear:
- Full-time A-level education at sixth form college ✓
- Standard college education (not employer-funded) ✓
- Not married ✓

A-levels are an approved non-advanced qualification, so Alex meets the education requirement. Now let me move to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(Since he's in full-time approved education, the key question is whether he's also working long hours alongside his studies. Part-time or casual work alongside studies is fine - it's only 24+ hours per week that would be an issue.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's just focused on his studies full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't work, so that requirement is met. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right, such as:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (in his own name)

Or to put it simply: **Is Alex receiving any of these benefits for himself?** (Yes/No)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any such benefits. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - since Alex is in full-time A-level education (not an apprenticeship), this requirement is straightforward:

**Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship?** 

Based on what you've told me (he's studying A-levels at sixth form college), I believe the answer is no - he's not in an apprenticeship. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - no, he's not doing an apprenticeship. He's just doing his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Now let me move to the next important check - your residency status:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. There are several possible paths - let me ask you the key question:

**Which of these applies to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and if so, I'd need to check if you're working, studying, job-seeking, or have sufficient resources)

4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** (or in certain qualifying countries)

Which best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK in Manchester, so you meet the residency requirement. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. There are a few ways you can be considered responsible:

**Which of these applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** (he lives with you at your home in Manchester)

2. **You contribute to his upkeep** (e.g., paying for his food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents - at least the equivalent of Child Benefit)

3. **You pay maintenance** (under a court order or agreement)

Based on what you mentioned earlier (Alex is living at home with you), I believe you live with him - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you clearly have responsibility for him. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check something important:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone applied for it?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (or anyone else) currently receiving Child Benefit for him?
- Has there been any dispute or discussion about who should claim?

Or is it just you making this claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me making this claim.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! There's no other claimant. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**

1. **In hospital** (staying in hospital)
2. **In care** (in a children's home or similar care facility)
3. **Fostered** (in a foster placement)
4. **Living normally** (at home with you or in other normal accommodation)

Based on what you've told me (he's at home with you), I believe it's option 4 - living normally. Can you confirm?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - he's just living normally at home with me. He's not in hospital, care, or fostered.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words - is the council funding/paying for his housing, food, or other care? Or are you paying for all of this yourself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm paying for everything myself. Alex just lives here at home with me as a normal family situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final piece of information I need. You're paying for everything yourself, and Alex lives with you as a normal family situation. Let me now provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Now let me provide you with the final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex!

**Summary:**
You meet all the eligibility criteria to claim Child Benefit for your 19-year-old son Alex. Because he is in full-time approved education (A-levels), living at home with you in the UK, and you're supporting him financially, you qualify.

**Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide documentation:**
   - Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your address (utility bill, council tax bill, etc.)

3. **Important note - High Income Child Benefit Charge:**
   - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be liable for the High Income Child Benefit Charge (a tax charge)
   - Even if you're affected, you should still claim - you can claim the benefit and manage the tax separately

4. **Payment frequency:**
   - Normally paid every 4 weeks
   - Can be weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain other benefits

**Useful Links:**
- [How to claim Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- [Child Benefit rates](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/rates)
- [High Income Child Benefit Charge](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/tax-charge)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?

reasonings: Alex is 19 years old and meets all Child Benefit eligibility requirements: (1) He is in full-time approved education (A-levels at sixth form college), which is non-advanced education meeting the 12+ hours supervised study requirement; (2) He is not working 24+ hours per week - he doesn't work at all; (3) He is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right; (4) He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) You normally live in the UK (Manchester); (6) You are responsible for him - you live with him; (7) No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him; (8) He is living normally at home with you; (9) The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for your son Alex. He meets all the criteria as a 19-year-old in approved full-time education (A-levels), living at home with you in the UK, with no other claimant and no council funding involved."
